claims.text: The CrFeCoNiAl alloy is a homogeneous, single-phase metallic solid solution.
Above 900 °C, aluminum is selectively oxidized in single-phase CrFeCoNiAl.
Selective aluminum oxidation produces a continuous, coherent α-Al2O3 surface scale.
The α-Al2O3 scale resists cracking, spallation, and rapid growth under oxidative conditions.
CrFeCoNiMn develops unstable, cracked oxide scales under analogous oxidation conditions.
The instability of the oxide on CrFeCoNiMn is caused by oxidation kinetics that differ from those of CrFeCoNiAl.
The proposed controlled comparison exposes CrFeCoNiAl and CrFeCoNiMn to oxidation at 950 °C in air.
The exposure includes controlled oxygen-partial-pressure cycling.
The proposed exposure lasts 100–200 hours and includes periodic thermal cycling.
The proposed α-Al2O3 scale has good lattice matching with the CrFeCoNiAl substrate.
Low oxygen diffusivity and good lattice matching minimize stress accumulation at the oxide/metal interface.
The Al-containing alloy is predicted to develop a slow-growing, adherent alumina scale.
The Mn-containing baseline is predicted to develop a nonuniform, cracked, and spalled oxide scale.
Competing diffusion or intermetallic interactions may affect oxide-scale integrity.
Failure of CrFeCoNiAl to form continuous, coherent α-Al2O3, or behavior comparable to the cracked, spalled, or rapidly growing Mn baseline, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The exposure is repeatedly described as isothermal, but it is also specified to include periodic or cyclic thermal oxidation. A single exposure cannot be strictly isothermal while its temperature is being cycled unless separate isothermal and cyclic test arms are defined.
